questions.question: Fundamental Rights are contained in which range of Articles of the Constitution?
questions.explanation:
Part III, Fundamental Rights, covers Articles 12 to 35.
Articles 5-11 deal with Citizenship, 36-51 with Directive Principles, and 52-78 with the Union Executive.

questions.question: Fundamental Rights are said to be 'justiciable'. What does this mean?
options: They can be enforced through the courts
They are only moral guidelines for the State
They can be changed by the President alone
They apply only during an emergency
questions.explanation:
Justiciable means a person can go to court (Supreme Court under Article 32, High Court under Article 226) if these rights are violated.
Directive Principles, not Fundamental Rights, are non-justiciable guidelines. The President cannot change them alone, and they apply at all times.

questions.question: What is the present status of the Right to Property in India?
options: A Directive Principle of State Policy
questions.explanation:
After the 44th Amendment (1978), the Right to Property is a constitutional or legal right under Article 300A in Part XII. It is no longer a Fundamental Right.
Article 19(1)(f) and Article 31 were removed, and it is not a Directive Principle.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act removed the Right to Property from the list of Fundamental Rights?
questions.explanation:
The 44th Amendment (1978), passed by the Janata government, removed the Right to Property.
The 42nd added Fundamental Duties, the 86th added the Right to Education (Article 21A), and the 73rd dealt with Panchayati Raj.

questions.question: Which Fundamental Rights cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency?
questions.explanation:
After the 44th Amendment (1978), the right to move courts for enforcing Article 20 (protection in respect of conviction for offences) and Article 21 (life and personal liberty) cannot be suspended under Article 359.
The enforcement of the other listed rights can be suspended during a National Emergency.

questions.question: According to Article 12, which of the following is included in 'the State'?
options: Only Parliament and the State Legislatures
The Government and Parliament of India, the Government and Legislature of each State, and all local and other authorities
Only the Union and State Governments
questions.explanation:
Article 12 includes the Government and Parliament of India, the Government and Legislature of each State, and all local or other authorities within India or under the control of the Government of India.
The other options are too narrow.

questions.question: Under Article 13, which of the following is included in the meaning of 'law'?
questions.explanation:
Article 13(3) says 'law' includes any ordinance, order, bye-law, rule, regulation, notification, and custom or usage having the force of law.
Contracts, manifestos and editorials do not have the force of law.

questions.question: Which Article gives the High Courts the power to issue writs for enforcing Fundamental Rights?
questions.explanation:
Article 226 gives the High Courts writ powers.
Article 32 gives this power to the Supreme Court, Article 368 deals with amending the Constitution, and Article 143 with the President seeking the Supreme Court's advice.

questions.question: Who chaired the Constituent Assembly's Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribal and Excluded Areas?
questions.explanation:
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel chaired this Advisory Committee.
Nehru chaired the Union Powers and Union Constitution Committees, Ambedkar the Drafting Committee, and Rajendra Prasad the Rules of Procedure and Steering Committees.

questions.question: Fundamental Rights mainly protect individuals against the actions of:
questions.explanation:
Most Fundamental Rights limit the power of the State, which is why Article 12 defines 'the State'. A few rights, such as Article 17, also apply against private individuals.
They are not limited to companies, foreign countries or religious bodies.
